title: Bookshop spare-room decision (fictional)
question: For the next three months, how should the neighbourhood bookshop use its spare room?
context: FICTIONAL CASE ONLY. A neighbourhood bookshop has a spare room. Stated options for the next three months: (1) paid workshops, (2) quiet reading room, (3) keep as storage. One staff member has five hours a week available. Demand and budget are unknown. No personal files, integrations or real business data were used. All figures and local demand claims are absent by design; assumptions are marked uncertain. Recommendation deliberately left empty. Shared constraints (not room-use options): one staff member has five hours a week; demand and budget are unknown. Comparison lenses when ready (attach under options, not as root siblings): revenue/contribution over 3 months; staff-hour fit within 5 h/week; budget/setup risk; learning value; ops/storage value preserved; reversibility after 3 months. Evidence boundary: only the fictional brief was used — no sales figures, demographics, competitor events, cost quotes, interviews, or personal/business integrations; no numbers invented. Sources: user-supplied fictional case; public Strategy Canvas repository for method/runtime only.
nextQuestion: Which consequential unknown would you rather resolve first: likely workshop demand, reading-room footfall, or storage value of the room?

nodes.label: Use of spare room (3 months)
nodes.notes:
Mode: explore mutually exclusive primary uses for the next three months; leave choice open.

First-split check (method.md choice-tree rule): root children answer only which primary room use to pursue. Shared criteria, staffing/budget constraints and evidence boundaries live in session context and these root notes — not as sibling cards.

Parent question / universe: primary use of the spare room for the next three months among the three stated options. Horizon: three months. Excluded for now: permanent renovation, selling the space, long leases, multi-use hybrids as a fourth primary category (hybrids noted under options if useful).

Grouping basis: primary room use (what the room is mainly for).

Sibling boundaries:
- Workshops: scheduled, ticketed learning events as primary use.
- Reading room: quiet sit-and-read space as primary use (may be free or lightly charged; charging is a variant, not a separate top option).
- Storage: room held for stock/ops storage; no public programme.

These three exhaust the user's stated choice set. Overlap: a workshop evening in an otherwise reading room is a hybrid — primary-placement by intended main use for the three-month trial; secondary uses in option notes.

Constraints from the brief (also in context): one staff member, five hours/week; demand unknown; budget unknown. Implications remain under each option.

Shared comparison lenses (not root children): revenue/contribution; staff-hour fit; budget/setup risk; learning value; ops/storage value; reversibility. Detail previously held under Shared criteria / Evidence boundary is preserved in context and option branches.

Draft / unreviewed exploration — structural first-split corrected; not a certified recommendation.

nodes.label: Paid workshops
nodes.notes:
Primary use: ticketed workshops in the spare room for three months.

Proposed mechanism: events create incremental revenue and footfall that may lift book sales; requires marketing, hosting capacity and enough paying demand.

Depends on: topics people will pay for, price, frequency feasible in 5 staff hours/week, materials/setup cost, and whether the room suits groups.

Proposed alternative, not a recommendation. Provenance: proposed from the stated case only.

nodes.label: How workshops could help
nodes.notes:
Causal sketch (unverified):
1) Attract paying attendees → workshop fee income.
2) Attendees browse/buy books → ancillary retail uplift.
3) Recurring programme builds local habit → repeat visits.

Break conditions: weak topic/price fit; marketing reach too small; staff hours consumed by prep/cleanup with little surplus; room capacity/ambiance poor for groups; cannibalises quiet browsing.

No demand or margin data in the brief.

nodes.label: 5 staff hours/week limit
nodes.notes:
Known constraint from brief: one staff member has five hours a week.

Implication (inference): feasible workshop cadence is likely low (e.g. one short session per week or fortnight) once prep, hosting, cleanup and bookings are included. Exact hours per workshop unknown — mark as gap.

Basis: stated constraint + inference about event ops. Not measured.

nodes.label: Paying demand unknown
nodes.notes:
Budget and demand unknown per brief.

Consequential gap: whether enough locals will pay at a price that covers materials, staff time and room opportunity cost.

Possible cheap checks (proposals, not instructions to run): waitlist interest for 1–2 topics; ask regulars; look at similar local event prices (public, if researched later). No check run in this session.

nodes.label: Setup & materials budget unknown
nodes.notes: Budget unknown. Workshops may need chairs, materials, insurance, payment tooling, or guest facilitator fees. Without a budget ceiling, financial viability cannot be assessed. Keep as explicit gap.

nodes.label: Quiet reading room
nodes.notes:
Primary use: quiet space for sitting and reading for three months.

Proposed mechanism: better dwell time and hospitality deepen loyalty and may increase browse-to-buy; possibly a small seat fee or membership, or free as amenity.

Depends on: whether people want a quiet sit-space here, supervision needs within 5 hours/week, furniture/fit-out cost, and theft/noise/ops risk.

Proposed alternative, not a recommendation.

nodes.label: How a reading room could help
nodes.notes:
Causal sketch (unverified):
1) Comfortable quiet space → longer visits.
2) Longer visits → more discovery and purchases / habit.
3) Distinctive amenity → word of mouth in the neighbourhood.

Break conditions: dwell without purchase; needs constant supervision the 5 hours cannot cover; space feels unused; fit-out cost high vs three-month horizon; conflicts with stock/ops needs.

No footfall or conversion data in the brief.

nodes.label: Supervision vs 5 hours/week
nodes.notes:
If the room must be supervised whenever open, five staff hours/week caps opening hours tightly unless the main shop floor already covers sightlines, or access is by appointment.

Unknown: can the room be left open unsupervised during shop hours? That single fact changes feasibility a lot.

nodes.label: Sit-and-read demand unknown
nodes.notes:
Demand unknown. Locals may prefer cafés, libraries or home. A reading room's value might be social/brand rather than direct revenue — still needs a success metric for three months.

Possible cheap checks: observe how often people ask to sit; temporary chairs for two weeks; ask regulars. None run here.

nodes.label: Fit-out budget unknown
nodes.notes: Budget unknown. Chairs, lighting, rugs, signage, accessibility tweaks may be needed. Low-cost trial possible in principle, but cost ceiling is unspecified.

nodes.label: Keep as storage
nodes.notes:
Primary use: continue/hold as storage for stock and operations for three months.

Proposed mechanism: protects ops capacity and avoids committing scarce staff hours and unknown budget to an unproven public use; preserves optionality to decide later with better information.

Trade-off: forgoes learning and possible revenue/loyalty from a public use during the window.

Proposed alternative (including 'no action'), not a recommendation.

nodes.label: How storage could help
nodes.notes:
Causal sketch:
1) Reliable storage → smoother stock handling / less shop-floor clutter.
2) No new programme → staff hours stay available for core retail.
3) Delay commitment → decide after learning more about demand/budget.

Break conditions: storage value is low (room barely used); opportunity cost of empty public potential is high; three-month window is uniquely good for a trial (e.g. seasonal events) — none of these are established in the brief.

nodes.label: Opportunity cost of not trying
nodes.notes:
Keeping storage means not running a three-month learning trial. That is only costly if a cheap trial would have revealed valuable demand. With demand unknown, the opportunity cost itself is unknown.

This is the core tension with the other two options.

nodes.label: Fits the 5-hour constraint
nodes.notes: Basis: storage as primary use does not inherently require a new weekly programme, so it is the least demanding of the three options on the stated five staff hours/week. 'Supported' here means consistency with the stated constraint, not proof that storage is best overall.

decision.rationale: Choice deliberately left open. First-split corrected so root children are only the three primary room uses; shared constraints and evidence limits sit in context. Branch analysis under each option is preserved. No ranking until you want to compare or deepen one branch.
uncertainties: Paying demand for workshops is unknown
Sit-and-read demand / unsupervised access is unknown
Budget ceiling for fit-out or materials is unknown
True storage value of the room is unknown
Hours required per workshop or per open reading-room hour are unknown
nextSteps: Optional: deepen one branch (workshops, reading room, or storage)
Optional: pick one cheap evidence check before committing the room
Optional: when ready, compare the three on the shared criteria
